newsitem.title: UK: Summary of expectations for UK 1996/97 budget.
newsitem.headline: Summary of expectations for UK 1996/97 budget.

text.p: The following is a selection of institutions' and economists' expectations and wishlists for chancellor Kenneth Clarke's budget to be delivered on Tuesday November 26.
Most of the forecasts were drawn up prior to October's unexpectedly high public sector debt repayment of 4.4 bln stg.
THE CONFEDERATION OF BRITISH INDUSTRY
* The government should trim its real spending target by two billion stg.
* Tax cuts should amount to only around one billion stg.

* "What we want is a budget that delivers a sound fiscal position. The Chancellor should have prudence as a watchword," said Andrew Buxton, chairman of Barclays Bank Plc and the CBI's economic affairs committee.
TRADES UNION CONGRESS
* The government should adopt investment and employment measures costing around three bln stg.
* This should include 1.0 bln stg invested in social housing, school buildings and urban regeneration creating up to 30,000 jobs and a 1.4 bln stg "back to work" scheme.
BRITISH CHAMBERS OF COMMERCE

* Chancellor Clarke should not cut taxes, given the strength of the third quarter BCC economic survey which showed 45 percent of manufacturing firms believed profitability would improve in the next 12 months.
INSTITUTE FOR FISCAL STUDIES/GOLDMAN SACHS
* Tax cuts of around 3.0 bln stg expected, paid for by cuts in government spending plans for fiscal 1997-8.
* Budget will forecast a drop in the PSBR to 21.7 bln stg in 1997-8, 2.8 percent of GDP, and to zero by 1999-2000.
* Government likely to cut public investment plans to help finance tax cuts.
* The Chancellor could start to remove the tax advantages of Profit Related Pay if he wanted to cut taxes more aggressively.
INSTITUTE OF DIRECTORS
* Although there should be no tax cuts, the IOD expects Clarke to give away one to two bln stg.
* It would like to see seven bln stg off the 1997-98 Control Total for government spending, taking it down to 253.2 bln stg.
* The IOD says this can be done using the five bln stg contingency reserves and taking advantage of the likelihood inflation in 1997-8 will be lower than orginally assumed.
* "There is clearly a strong political pressure to cut taxes but if he goes too far it will be inflationary and imprudent," said Tim Melville-Ross, the IOD's Director General.
ADAM SMITH INSTITUTE
* Capital gains tax should be abolished or phased out.
* Inheritance Tax should be ended.
* Duties on alcohol to come down.
* There should be no increase in Insurance Premium Tax.
ROGER BOOTLE, RECENTLY CHOSEN AS "WISE MAN" AND CHIEF ECONOMIST, HSBC MARKETS
* Clarke may opt for net tax cuts of around 2.0 to 3.0 bln stg, with the main measures being a one pence cut in the standard rate of income tax and a small widening of the 20 pence band.
* The threshold for Inheritance Tax could be raised and excise duty on alcohol could be sharply reduced.
* The centrepiece may be a forward plan for tax cuts over several years, bringing the standard rate down to 20 pence.
DEUTSCHE MORGAN GRENFELL

* If the Chancellor succeeds in making two bln stg of spending cuts for FY 1997/98, he can afford two-three bln stg of tax cuts and still pencil in a PSBR around 22 bln stg, lower than the summer economic forecast.
PHILIP SHAW, UNION DISCOUNT
* We may see a one pence reduction in the basic rate of tax and increased allowances.

* This is contingent on Clarke making expenditure savings and raising taxes in other areas such as another one percent on tobacco and road fuel tax or a reduction on tax relief on profit related pay. * We suggest the Control Total will be set at 266-267 bln stg -- a one to two billion stg reduction in planned spending.
-- Jennifer Scott, London newsroom +44 171 542 7708
